It compiled successfully. The deprecation note is harmless (likely `CSVFormat.Builder.create(CSVFormat)` or similar being marked deprecated in favor of another entry point), and the build still reports "compiled OK".

I wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVPrinterAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class covering `CSVPrinter`'s documented contract:

- Constructor: null-argument `NullPointerException`s, header auto-printed without being counted, `IOException` propagation when the header can't be written.
- `print`/`println`: `String.valueOf` semantics (including `null`), quoting of delimiter-containing values, record-count semantics, `IOException` propagation.
- `printRecord`/`printRecords` (varargs, `Iterable`, `Stream`): single-record vs. nested-array-as-multiple-records behavior per the javadoc examples, empty-input boundary cases, record counting.
- `printComment`: no-op when disabled, marker+space formatting, multi-line splitting, exceptions when enabled.
- `printHeaders`/`printRecords(ResultSet...)`: using `java.lang.reflect.Proxy`-based fake `ResultSet`/`ResultSetMetaData` (to avoid implementing the huge JDBC interfaces by hand) to verify header/data output and that headers are excluded from `getRecordCount()`, plus `SQLException` propagation.
- `flush`/`close`/`close(boolean)`: delegation to the underlying `Flushable`/`Closeable`, honoring the flush flag, and `IOException` propagation.
